claim: The repo already has a v1 dashboard protobuf schema, but it is a view/response schema (RunSummary, LiveResponse, TracesResponse, GoldEvalResponse) that is memory-benchmark-specific and heavily stringly-typed, not a generic source-of-truth trace model.

The existing schema uses JSON-in-string escape hatches for structured data (report_json, params_json, roles_detail_json, answer_json, debug_artifact), which is the anti-pattern to avoid for query-critical fields.
Closed-vocabulary fields are modeled as bare strings (kind, status, operation, severity, transition, final_status) instead of enums.

OpenTelemetry is deprecating the Span Events API in 2026, consolidating on 'events are logs with names' emitted via the Logs API and correlated to spans by context; guidance is to prefer independent event records over attributes hung on a span.

Span Links model non-hierarchical, multi-directional, cross-trace relationships and are the correct mechanism for fan-out, fan-in/batch, async messaging (producer/consumer), and retry — cases where a strict one-parent tree fails; OTel messaging conventions use links not parent-child.
Protobuf field numbers are identity: never change or reuse them; use `reserved` for deleted numbers/names; adding fields is always safe; adding an arm to an existing oneof is forward-incompatible.
Never put trace_id/span_id as metric attributes — it causes cardinality explosion and makes metrics unusable; correlation belongs on events, not aggregates.

Protobuf messages are not self-delimiting; the standard append-stream framing is a varint length prefix per message (writeDelimitedTo/parseDelimitedFrom; prost encode_length_delimited) — the typed structural analog of JSONL.

Connect-Web with protobuf-es is the current best browser choice for protobuf/gRPC, supports server-streaming via for-await, needs no translating proxy, and tree-shakes to small bundles; the repo already generates debugger_pb.ts via protobuf-es.
Event sourcing: append-only immutable events are source of truth; current state / views are projections (folds) rebuildable by replay — enabling new views over old runs with no re-execution.

The repo already has a source-hash staleness gate with an escape hatch (SYMEM_IGNORE_SOURCE_HASH), which generalizes into a first-class ArtifactProvenance header (source sha256, schema/version, complete flag, invalidated_by) with hash-based cache invalidation.
evidence: project memory answer-only-local-rerank-rig: 'path->git dep refactor trips the answer-only manifest staleness gate -> need SYMEM_IGNORE_SOURCE_HASH=1'; debugger.proto truncated bools lines 409/494/447

claim: The existing schema already stores pre-computed durations (TraceWaterfallBlock start_ms/end_ms/duration_ms, QueueTiming wait_ms/run_ms/total_ms) which should instead be derived from matched start/end events with authoritative timestamps.

The existing schema already leans toward cursor-paged fetch for history (ArtifactResponse offset/limit/total, TraceEventStream truncated) which should be formalized as opaque-cursor pagination separated by record type.

The build already compiles the proto via prost_build with a versioned package path membench.dashboard.v1, so a parallel membench.trace.v1 package for the generic trace model fits the existing toolchain.
evidence: build.rs (prost_build compile_protos on proto/membench/dashboard/v1/debugger.proto); src/dashboard_proto.rs module path membench.dashboard.v1

claim: The observability tier converges on a 5-level object spine: Project → Dataset/Example(gold) → Experiment/Run → Trace → Span, with Score attachable at any level. An Experiment = the set of Traces (one per Example) plus the Scores over them.
evidence: LangSmith 'An Experiment is a set of runs (one per example) plus feedback scores'; Langfuse 'For each DatasetItem a DatasetRunItem & a Trace are created' — docs.langchain.com/langsmith/manage-datasets, langfuse.com/docs/evaluation/experiments/data-model

claim: Langfuse has the most explicit/typed data model: Trace → typed Observations (generation/span/event/tool-call/retrieval, nestable) → Session; Score attaches to trace/observation/session/dataset-run; DatasetItem→DatasetRun→DatasetRunItem joins item↔trace.

Braintrust owns the best regression/comparison UX: select two experiments → Compare → side-by-side diff of improved/regressed/same vs a baseline, Diff-mode toggle, filter bar accepting natural language or BTQL, inline LLM-judge chain-of-thought per row. Experiments table = one row/run with score averages, error counts, duration, token usage, cost.

LangSmith comparison view supports selecting any number of runs; 3 table modes (Compact/Full/Diff-vs-reference); per-score heatmap with user-set high/mid/low red-green threshold; Repetition Summary for variance; per-example columns for cost, token counts, latency, status.

W&B Weave has a first-class Leaderboard object: rows = models/versions, columns = (evaluation run × scoring fn × summary metric such as mean or true_fraction); shareable across org for regression tracking. Core objects: Op, Call/Trace, Dataset, Evaluation, Scorer, Model, Leaderboard.

Phoenix data model is literally OpenTelemetry/OpenInference OTLP spans with semantic kinds (LLM, retriever, tool, chain); retriever spans expose retrieved documents + relevance, and Annotations (span_id, name, annotator_kind, result) attach to spans/traces. Closest existing model to retrieval-evidence.

Ragas is the only tool whose core objects are retrieval-evidence-shaped: each Sample = {question, retrieved_contexts, answer, ground_truth}, and its headline metrics are context precision, context recall, context entities recall, faithfulness, answer relevancy — presupposing a retrieved-vs-gold comparison. But these are aggregate numbers, not per-evidence-piece per-question coverage UI.

HELM separates per-instance metric stats (PerInstanceStats / per_instance_stats.json) from aggregates (stats.json) as first-class serialized artifacts, plus ScenarioState logging every request/response, enabling drill from leaderboard cell → per-instance → exact request. RunSpec = scenario + adapter + metrics.

Inspect (UK AISI) models Task = {Dataset of Samples, Solver(s), Scorer}; Sample = input+target+metadata; Scorer declares metrics e.g. @scorer(metrics=[accuracy(), stderr()]). Log viewer shows per-sample transcript + chronological EVENTS (model call, tool call, scoring) not just a span tree. Run-vs-run comparison is dataframe-native (evals_df one row/run, samples_df cross-run per-sample).

Humanloop uses immutable content-hashed Dataset Versions so every evaluation is provably tied to the exact set of Datapoints (inputs+messages+target); each Evaluation links to a specific Dataset Version. (Analogous to the project's existing source-hash gating.)

OpenAI Evals is a thin registry/JSONL format (no OSS UI): eval YAML + samples.jsonl where each line is {input:[chat msgs], ideal:...}; naming <eval_name>.<split>.<version> groups comparable evals; CompletionFn is the system under test. Vercel AI SDK / Evalite is code-first eval-driven-development, evals as Vitest-style test files in-repo, model-agnostic via AI Gateway.

Convergent cost surface: tokens+cost+latency are measured at the leaf (generation/span) and rolled up to trace then run; every observability-tier product shows per-run cost as a column (LangSmith, Braintrust, Langfuse, Weave, Opik).
Convergent trace drilldown = waterfall/tree of timed typed spans with model calls at the leaves; Langfuse renders the observation tree as a waterfall to show where time and tokens were spent.
evidence: langfuse.com/docs/observability/overview; braintrust/phoenix/opik/weave all expose per-testcase span trees

claim: For OUR memory benchmark, the differentiated view no competitor can render is a per-question gold-evidence coverage matrix (rows=gold evidence pieces; columns=retrieved?/rank/survived-rerank?/in-context?/cited?) plus a 4-lane (provider/memory/recall/judge) waterfall where the recall lane shows retrieve→dedup→rerank→context-cut with evidence dropping out at each stage — because competitors' core objects are not evidence-piece-shaped.
evidence: Synthesis: Ragas gives only aggregate context precision/recall; Phoenix shows docs in a span but not per-evidence-piece per-question coverage — docs.ragas.io, arize.com/docs/phoenix

claim: Current top-level IA is already a 2-mode split (Leaderboard vs Debugger), toggled by F1/F2 and rendering exactly one at a time — recommend promoting to a 3-workspace spine (Leaderboard/Runs/Lab).

State is URL-addressed and shareable via hash router: #/debug/<run-id>/<subscreen>, and parse() is forgiving of subscreen order — this is the invariant that lets one object (a run) be viewed by all three personas.
The Debugger already implements master-detail: persistent 248px registry tree (master) + run-scoped tab bar (detail) for overview/questions/compare/traces/gold-coverage/live/tuner.

Questions drilldown already does list+filters (verdict/qtype/search) + a lazy-loaded per-question debug drawer, but filter state is component-local $state (not in URL), so tiles can't deep-link into it and views aren't shareable.

Every summary tile should become a filtered drilldown into Questions; verdict filters (correct/wrong/abstain/error) and per-qtype cells already exist as data (per_question_type on RunSummary) but are only reachable by manual chip clicks.
evidence: dashboard/src/sections/Questions.svelte verdict/qtype filters; dashboard/src/lib/types.ts RunSummary.per_question_type; CategoryHeat.svelte

Live monitoring (observe) is strong — 2s polling, queue segments (queued/running/succeeded/failed/dead), per-stage progress — but there is no act surface (no stop/pause/resume/retry); Tuner only previews a copyable script, so the operator loop is not closed.
